summary: Lunarnav is a website designed to help ensure safe, accident-free landings—and to prevent accidents—on the southern side of the Moon.
details: It works by letting you select your desired landing site and your spacecraft; it then provides the probability of a successful landing and guidance on how to execute it. The system leverages data from previous lunar missions—such as Artemis II and Apollo 13—and uses statistical analysis to determine how to land at a specific location. It makes a significant impact by helping NASA engineers and astronauts land on the Moon while minimizing risk. We utilized specific hardware and a base-44 numerical system to develop the project. It also serves to help those outside the aerospace industry understand how the process works and the immense challenges involved in reaching the lunar surface. The team’s goal was to ensure the system is easy to explain and understand, while remaining genuinely useful.
